name: CAPP / IBS-DMAG
full_name: Center for Axion and Precision Physics Research axion experiments
summary: A Korean IBS cavity-axion program using several magnet and cavity configurations; this archive groups the series instead of treating each run number as a separate collaboration.
detection_principle: Axions convert to resonant microwaves in a strong field; cryogenic copper cavities, high-field magnets and low-noise amplifiers improve weak-power detection.

status.label: Multiphase project: completed experiments alongside further construction / design
status.evidence: 2024 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: Extensive search for axion dark matter over 1 GHz with CAPP’s Main Axion eXperiment

collaboration.name: CAPP / IBS-DMAG Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

key_parameters.name: Flagship configuration
key_parameters.value: 12 T magnet, 320 mm bore, 37 L copper cavity

phases.name: CAPP multiple-cavity / magnet approaches
phases.description: CAPP-8TB, 9T, 12T and other configurations are distinguished by publication.

phases.name: ACTION
phases.description: Toroidal-cavity and toroidal-field R&D, not counted again here.

results.summary: A 2024 paper reports a high-sensitivity scan above 1 GHz.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
